steps.message:
### Root Cause

When releasing a book via `Book.finalize_release`, two separate `Book` instances for the same database row were loaded and updated inside one transaction:

1. `book = find(id)` loaded the first `Book` instance.
2. `marker = ReleaseMarker.for(id)` queried `Book.drafts.find_by(id: book_id)` and wrapped a **second** `Book` instance still holding the old working `title` in memory.
3. Inside the transaction, `book.update!(title: ..., subtitle: ...)` updated `title` on the first instance, and `marker.publish!` called `@book.update!(published: true)` on the second instance.
4. On transaction commit, ActiveRecord deduplicated `after_update_commit` callbacks by record identity and ran `Book::Recap#write_recap` only on the last-saved instance in the transaction (`marker`'s `@book`), which had `published: true` in memory alongside the stale working `title`. That wrote `{ title: <working title>, published: true }` into `Rails.cache` until the book was saved again or the recap expired.

### Fix

- Updated `ReleaseMarker.for` and `Book.finalize_release` (`app/models/release_marker.rb`, `app/models/book/release.rb`) so `finalize_release` passes the loaded `Book` instance directly to `ReleaseMarker.for` (while keeping `ReleaseMarker.for` compatible with book IDs), avoiding a second stale `Book` instance in the release transaction.
- Hardened `Book::Recap#write_recap` (`app/models/book/recap.rb`) to read the committed `title` and `published` attributes from the database when writing the per-book recap cache entry (`["book_recap", id]`) with the configured `Rails.application.config.x.recap.expires_in` TTL, ensuring multi-instance updates in a transaction can never cache stale in-memory attributes.
- Added model and integration tests (`test/models/book/recap_test.rb`, `test/controllers/books/releases_controller_test.rb`) covering book release, ordinary renames, per-book recap isolation, multi-instance transactions, rollbacks, and configured expiration schedules.
